items.text: The invoice export CSV format was revised on 2026-11-03: the initial comma-separated output (which showed everything in column A and garbled Müller as MÃ¼ller in German-locale Excel) was replaced by semicolon (`;`) separation with a UTF-8 BOM. Finance confirmed it works; the agent verified BOM bytes `ef bb bf`, the `;` split and intact `Müller & Söhne GmbH`, but did not open it in Excel. German-locale Excel requires a semicolon separator and UTF-8 BOM. Commit 707eb86 ships scripts/export_invoices.py with this semicolon + UTF-8 BOM output.

scripts/export_invoices.py (usage: `python scripts/export_invoices.py DB_PATH OUT_CSV`) exports the `invoices` table of a TinyDB db.json to CSV with columns `number,customer,amount,due_date`, one row per invoice plus a header. It opens the DB read-only, leaves missing fields blank, ignores extra fields, and exits 1 if the DB file is missing and 2 on wrong arguments. It was added on 2026-11-03 at Finance's request. scripts/sample_db.json is a sample DB (including an extra `customers` table to confirm only invoices is exported, and a fourth invoice INV-1004 with a Müller customer). The script and sample were committed on branch `invoices-export` as 707eb86 (not pushed).

items.text: TinyDB v4.0.0 was released on 2020-05-02 with upgrade notes and changelog, followed by v4.1.0 (2020-05-07), v4.1.1 (2020-05-08) and v4.2.0 (2020-10-03). v4.1.0 features: an `access_mode` flag for JSONStorage (#297) and a noop (empty) query operation (#313); custom doc_ids during insertion were implemented later (#303).

Table.update and Table.remove now skip missing doc_ids instead of raising KeyError (2026-05-21, #616, fixes #591). IDs are filtered inside the updater before side effects so operations are atomic and consistent with Table.get; upsert dropped its unreachable except KeyError branch. Previously a mix of existing and missing IDs half-applied updates in place because documents are shared by reference.

Queries are treated as cacheable by default. In v4.6.0 callable queries broke because `is_cacheable` was expected on every query; fixed in v4.6.1 (2022-01-18, 1fa99fb, fixes #454) so `is_cacheable` is called only if present, otherwise the query is cacheable. Operations like `map` are marked noncacheable (#445).

Query/table features added over 2020-2022: `map` query operation (#445), `fragment` search (#300), `update_multiple`, `doc_id` handling in `upsert()` (#395/#394), and `insert_multiple` accepting `Document` instances (#389).

items.text: Table refactor in Jan-Feb 2020 to simplify the API and make method semantics explicit: `Table.contains` accepts a single doc ID only (avoiding ambiguous list semantics), `process_docs` was removed, the table stores the next ID instead of the last ID, `len(table)` performance improved, internal read/update methods were renamed, and default cache capacity and default table name became configurable. Regressions after this new architecture were fixed Feb-May 2020: document ID generation, `len(db)` with empty databases, doc ID conversion during updates, regex handling of non-string values, counting docs in an empty db (#307), next doc ID calculation on an existing table (#314); support for evaluating queries without a test was dropped.

Decision (2026-08-08, #617, fixes #516): Table.search() results share structure with the query cache (shallow list copy), so mutating returned documents corrupts later identical searches. This is documented as a caveat (also in usage.rst) rather than fixed, because a deep copy costs 150-4000x on the read hot path.

The codebase invests in typing: PEP 561 compatibility via `py.typed` (2020-11), better type completion for PyCharm/VS Code/MyPy (#372), MyPy plugin config and docs, `Protocol` from typing_extensions for Python <=3.7, typing-extensions 4.x allowed (#447), variable annotations replacing type-hint comments, and MyPy error fixes.

Post-refactor fixes in Feb-May 2020: document ID generation, `len(db)` with empty databases, doc ID conversion during updates, regex handling of non-string values, and counting docs in an empty db (#307) were fixed. The next doc ID calculation on an existing table was fixed (#314). Support for evaluating queries without a test was dropped. | When: 2020-02-19 to 2020-05-07 | Involving: Markus Siemens | Regressions after the new architecture

items.text: TinyDB underwent a major architecture refactor for v4.0 (rationale in #284, Nov 2019, led by Markus Siemens): Python 2 support removed, `ujson` support deprecated, the deprecated element ID API removed, type annotations added, and subclassing helpers introduced as 'Extension Mechanisms'. Closes #250 and #103. Goal: simplify the codebase and provide extension mechanisms for the new architecture.

October 2026 query-correctness fixes: Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes/bytearray as sequences (is_sequence now uses collections.abc.Sequence; #641, fixes #638); regex flags are now part of the matches/search query hash so case-insensitive and case-sensitive searches no longer share a Table query-cache entry (#640, fixes #637).
tinydb released v3.12.0 on 2018-11-06 and v3.12.1 on 2018-11-09 (version bump commits by Markus Siemens). | When: 2018-11-06 to 2018-11-09 | Involving: Markus Siemens
